newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Swiss franc stars in low Hungary FX futures trade.
newsitem.headline: Swiss franc stars in low Hungary FX futures trade.

text.p: Trade on Hungary's currency futures markets was low on Thursday with the Swiss franc once again in focus and the rising German mark in a supporting role as the dollar fell on spot markets.

The Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) financial section posted a meagre 1.79 billion forints turnover while the much smaller Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) saw only one contract for June marks worth 171 million forints.

Long term contracts for the Swiss franc and mark accounted for almost all BCE trade. The September Swiss franc was most popular and firmed 80 fillers to 133.05 forints, while May strengthened a full two forints to 125.00.
The September mark also saw substantial trade, rising three fillers to 116.73.

Dealers believe relatively low interest in foreign currencies, notably in the Swiss franc, represent a good tool with which to speculate on the crawling peg devalution of the forint in longer term deals such as September and December.
From April the devaluation rate will be reduced to 1.1 percent per month from 1.2 percent.
The falling dollar on the spot market also made itself felt on the BSE, with May dollar prices falling 1.13 forints to 180.54 forints and December dropping 2.73 to 191.42.
Thursday's central bank midday fix for the three currencies was 122.28 forints for the Swiss franc, up 0.42, 104.85 for the mark, up 0.14 and 175.60 for dollar, unchanged.
